task.title: Discover all durable schedule intents
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/795 with deterministic full inventory before defining dispatch or automatic recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Return pending, cancelled, and claimed schedules in exact schedule-ID order after reopen.
Discover candidates from authoritative creation events in one SQLite read snapshot.
Exclude unrelated streams and return an empty list for an empty store.
Fail the whole query on invalid owning identities, malformed payloads, unsupported events, or impossible histories.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused integration test failed because ScheduleStore::list did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added insertion-order independence, reopen, all-status, unrelated-stream, malformed-candidate, and invalid-history tests.

attempts.diagnostic: Requiring callers to retain every exact ID prevented operational inspection, while a separate mutable index would duplicate event-log truth.
attempts.patch: Shared one fail-closed discovery projection between full inventory and due filtering, then applied query-specific ordering and filtering.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent and substantive hosted review found no discrete blocking bug at the merged head.
attempts.patch: Documented that inventory grants no mutation or execution authority and completed focused plus repository-wide verification.

outcome.summary: Callers can now inspect every durable one-shot schedule in stable exact-ID order from one authoritative read snapshot.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store

lessons: Add complete read-only inventory before operational execution so persisted state remains inspectable.
One authoritative snapshot prevents a result assembled from mutually inconsistent aggregate revisions.
Reuse discovery and projection while keeping full-inventory and due-order policy explicit at their call sites.
Malformed authoritative candidates must fail the entire inventory rather than disappear silently.
